thread:
maria: Quick follow-up from last night's incident — root cause was a KV-cache eviction pattern under bursty short-context traffic. We missed it in CI because our regression suite doesn't include the short-prefix heavy workload that triggered it.
ken: Can you link the postmortem? want to make sure action items tie back.
maria: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-12-kv-cache-tail-latency — see section 'replication trigger' and timeline. TL;DR: small requests w/ high qps + cache eviction = regen on hot paths.
ajay: Agree we need new evals. Proposing 3 additions: (1) prompt-set for short-context heavy QPS, (2) load-test scenario with bursty inter-arrival times, (3) a chaos drill that forces KV eviction on one node while measuring tail latency.
sarah: I can own the prompt-set. Will curate ~200 prompts that hit short-prefixs and repeat patterns. Target: 10k synthetic QPS run in staging. ETA 10 business days.
linda: I'll own the chaos drill run. Plan: simulate full-cache eviction by clearing prefix caches and then run the staged burst. Need a runbook entry and rollback steps. ETA: 7 business days to prepare, 14 to schedule with oncall.
ajay: I'll add the regression to the eval CI harness. Plan is to add a nightly job and a quick pre-deploy smoke. Job YAML sketch:```yaml
name: kv_cache_regression
schedule: nightly
load_profile: bursty_short_qps
metrics: [p99_latency, p999_latency, error_rate]
thresholds:
  p999_latency: 800ms
```
ajay: I'll target a PR in two weeks, unless we want it earlier as hotfix.
ken: Who's tracking these action items? we should add owners + due dates in the postmortem follow-up doc and our action tracker.
maria: I'll update the postmortem follow-up doc and add the owners + dates. Also adding a recurring item: "include bursty short-context scenario" to the core regression suite.
ops-bot: NOTE: action added to SRE tracker (#SRE-486) — owners: ajay/sarah/linda — due: 2026-04-02.
sarah: quick Q — for the prompt-set, do we include system messages + tool calls or just plain text? we should include both since tool-calling changes tokenization and cache behavior.
ajay: include both. definitely include tool-call patterns. Also include variable sequence lengths (4-64 tokens) to stress attention and KV reuse.
linda: For the chaos drill, request ops windows from platform — prefer low-traffic weekend. I'll draft runbook: steps to evict KV caches, validation commands, and rollback: scale-up or fallback to model-variant.
maria: Great. can everyone react with :white_check_mark: when they accept the owner/time? I'll consolidate into the follow-up doc after that.
ken: :white_check_mark:
ajay: :white_check_mark:
sarah: :white_check_mark: will start curation today
linda: :white_check_mark: will draft runbook by EOD Monday
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: none. Reminder: add pre-deploy smoke to pipeline before next canary.
maria: Thanks all — I'll update the postmortem follow-up with the owners and the SRE ticket link. We'll re-run the chaos drill in staging and add the regression to nightly; if p999 spikes > threshold we'll block canary.
ken: One more ask — can we add a short eval that runs during rollouts (low-sample) to catch regressions earlier? even 1k requests to the prompt-set could surface problems.
ajay: good idea. I'll add a pre-rollout sampling job.
maria: Done. Follow-up doc will include: action list, owners, ETA, runbooks, CI job names, and rollback policy. Closing thread when doc has updates.
